extracted.intended_audience: federal agency acquisition/procurement officials (acquisition executives, program managers, procurement staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for federal agencies to prepare time-phased implementation/action plans required by OMB Circular A-109 for major systems acquisitions, including policy, organizational, scheduling, and training items. Focused on producing an agency plan and implementing issuances for managing major system procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of acquisition executive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must designate an acquisition executive responsible for implementing A-109; OFPP provided and requested a current list of acquisition executives (contact names and phone numbers are included as examples). The acquisition executive approves implementing issuances and receives submission of agency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of major systems (cost thresholds and criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of major systems including cost threshold(s) and other criteria for major systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-phased plans must state the dollar threshold(s) and any other criteria an agency will use to designate a system as a 'major system.' Agencies gave examples in their plans (e.g., listed thresholds such as ADP over $10 million, construction over $10 million, tentative Labor threshold $500,000). The definition should be explicit and applied consistently across planning and implementing documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for identification and definition of mission areas and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule for identification and definition of mission areas and the process for gaining agency head approval of mission needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must include a timetable for identifying mission areas, defining mission needs, and documenting the process and authority by which the agency head (or designee) will approve mission needs that trigger the major systems acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and scheduling of agency-level implementing policy directives, regulations, and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and scheduling of agency implementing policy directives, regulations, and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should list the implementing issuances they will issue (departmental directives, administrative orders, regulations, guidance), and provide target dates for drafting, review, issuance, and when they will become operative. OFPP requested copies of such issuances as they are developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling of component-level implementing issuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling of component implementing policy directives, regulations, and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to agency-level issuances, plans should show schedules for subordinate/component directives and regulations, including coordination and promulgation steps at the component level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for assignment of program managers and development of program charters
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for assignment of program managers and development of charters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must describe how program managers will be selected/assigned, the authority and responsibilities given to them, and the process for developing formal program charters that define scope, responsibilities, and reporting relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for developing acquisition strategies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should describe standardized procedures and timelines for creating acquisition strategies for major systems, including tailoring approaches to the program, review/approval processes, and how strategies link to key decision points and program management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy regarding agency cost estimating capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy regarding agency cost estimating capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-phased plans should state agency policy on cost estimating (the capability, responsibility, and processes for producing credible cost estimates). This may include organizational responsibilities, tools/methods, review processes, and training or improvements needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates when policies will be operative and timing of first key decision point
rubrics_metrics.description: Date policies will be operative; e.g., when will all agency major systems begin with the first key decision point - approval of mission need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must give firm target dates when new policies and procedures will be in effect and indicate when the agency will begin applying the major-systems key decision framework (notably when the approval of mission need becomes the first key decision point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of agency personnel in new policies, procedures, and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Training of agency personnel in new policies, procedures and improvements in skills that are required; for example, program management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should include training programs, schedules, and target groups (e.g., program managers, procurement staff) to ensure personnel have the skills to implement A-109 processes and new issuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of time-phased action plan and sharing implementing issuances with OFPP
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of time-phased action plan by the specified deadline and provision of implementing directives to OFPP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies were required to submit time-phased implementation action plans by October 5, 1976 (example date from the memorandum). OFPP also requested copies of directives, circulars, procedures, or other issuances that will be used to implement A-109 prior to their promulgation so OFPP can review them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned sequence of implementation steps (draft, comment, revise, approval, publish, submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule of actions to implement A-109 including drafting implementing chapters/orders, requesting comments, revising, obtaining acquisition executive approval, publishing plan, and submitting to OFPP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many agencies provided a stepwise schedule as part of their plan (examples: draft chapter, request comments, make modifications, obtain acquisition executive approval, publish plan, submit plan to OFPP). Plans should reflect such a sequence with target dates for each step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scheduling of key decision points and associated implementing documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and scheduling of major system acquisition key decision points and the production/finalization of implementing documents (e.g., DoD restructuring of 5000.1/5000.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must identify the series of key decision points (including the initial approval of mission need), describe what documentation and reviews attach to each decision point, and schedule the completion of governing documents and procedures that establish the decision framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of proposed acquisitions to be treated as major systems and tailoring of planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of proposed acquisitions to be treated as major system acquisitions; major system acquisition planning and acquisition strategy tailoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should set out criteria and processes for deciding which proposed acquisitions are major systems, describe how acquisition planning will be performed for those systems, and indicate how acquisition strategies will be tailored for different program types (as HEW and others described).
